Benchmark code is public: bench.c on the fork's avx2 branch (10M-iteration phr_parse_request loop) and fukamachi.c on the fork's kazuho/expr/fukamachi-fast-http-bench branch.

corrections.claimed_speedup: bench.c: 3,900,156 -> 6,963,788 (1.79x); fukamachi.c: 4,807,692 -> 8,064,516 (1.68x). Page does not label the unit (higher is better; consistent with requests/second).

tier_reason: README #speed table gives the 8 Rust/C ratios exactly as claimed (0.680, 0.827, 1.023, 1.100, 1.185, 1.199, 1.482, 1.811) against pinned h2o/picohttpparser f4d94b48, and results/bench-compare.json holds the same values (large 0.6803, anchor 0.8267). The code is public (scripts/bench_compare.sh + scripts/bench_compare.c + scripts/bench_corpus.h), and GCC 16.2.0 -O2, rustc 1.96.1 opt-level=2/LTO/CGU1 and an i5-12400F are all stated (README + docs/methodology.md), which meets tier A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: C oracle: GCC 16.2.0 (w64devkit), anchor -O2 with C-side asserts live (NDEBUG unset), no -march so picohttpparser's SSE4.2/PCMPESTRI path is not compiled in; side tiers -O3 and -O3 -march=native via C_OPT. Rust: rustc 1.96.1, release profile opt-level=2, codegen-units=1, lto=true (side tiers RUSTFLAGS -C opt-level=3 / -C target-cpu=native).
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i5-12400F (12 logical CPUs), Windows (Git-Bash/MSYS2 userland), custom power scheme, no CPU pinning, whole-loop clock_gettime timer (no p50/p95/p99)
corrections.caveats: The two wins are against picohttpparser built -O2 without SSE4.2, i.e. its scalar path. In the same-session native tier (results/bench-compare-native.json: C -O3 -march=native vs Rust -C target-cpu=native, upstream bench.c request), C is 1.45x faster than Rust, so the 0.827 upstream-marker win flips to a loss once the baseline's SIMD path is on. At the -O3 tier, large headers is still a win (0.8165). In results/bench-compare.json, 6 of 8 rows, including large headers (0.6803), are flagged stability 'CHECK-spread>5%', not only the upstream-marker row the README flags. The author calls the numbers 'internal-engineering' and 'not portable'. The project pitches memory safety and parity with the C (133,352/133,352 differential cases), not speed: 6 of 8 workloads lose. Extremely new (created 2026-09-09, 2 stars, single author, no CI).

notes: Numbers and metadata check out (MIT, not a fork, 2 stars, last commit 2026-09-11, active). I kept this as confirm because the README does publish workload-specific wins against the named baseline, but it is borderline 'not faster': the wins exist only against scalar -O2 C and vanish against -march=native C. The orchestrator may want to tag it mixed or workload-specific, or drop it as not-faster.

tier_reason: The README #benchmark tables compare httppv1, httppv2 and picohttpparser at -O0 and -O3 and match the claimed numbers. The code is public (benchmarks/run.sh, bench-httppv2.c, bench-pico.c) and gcc 15.2.1 with -O0/-O3 is stated, but the CPU is given only as 'Ryzen 7 with 4.79GHz peek frequency', with no model. That makes it the project's own benchmark with partial methodology: tier C, not B (no peer review or independent suite).

corrections.claimed_speedup: At -O3: httppv2 (2.0.0) 8,893,776.12 req/s (1.124382s) vs picohttpparser 3,939,350.39 req/s (2.538490s), ~2.26x (derived from page data); httppv1 (1.0.0) 2,855,841.74 req/s (3.501595s), slower than pico at -O3. At -O0: httppv1 2,008,030.68 and httppv2 3,475,424.44 req/s vs picohttpparser 1,130,465.28 req/s.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 15.2.1 20251112; -O0 and -O3 only, no -march/-msse4.2 (benchmarks/run.sh), so picohttpparser's SSE4.2 fast path is not compiled in; picohttpparser is cloned unpinned from h2o master at run time
corrections.caveats: CPU given only as 'Ryzen 7' (no SKU); first-party benchmark, 5 runs averaged, clock()-based timing. The comparison is not like-for-like: picohttpparser runs its scalar path (no -msse4.2) while httpp calls libc memchr/strstr, which are SIMD in glibc. httpp also does far less validation: no token/CTL character checks on method, path or header names/values, no incomplete-request (-2) handling, and strstr over the input assumes NUL-termination. httpp is header-only and inlined into the bench TU, while pico is a separate TU. The -O0 rows are debug builds and should be ignored. Very new single-maintainer project (9 stars).

notes: I downgraded B to C: CPU model missing and the numbers are first-party, not an independent suite. Metadata checks out (MIT, not a fork, 9 stars, last commit 2025-12-21, active; releases 1.0.0 2025-11-29, 2.0.0 2025-12-05; benchmarks/httppv2.h is identical to the root httpp.h). The 2.26x is real on the page but inflated by the scalar-pico build and much lighter validation.
